newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's outlawed union body postpones strikes.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's outlawed union body postpones strikes.

text.p: South Korea's outlawed union organisation said on Tuesday it was abandoning its once-a-week strikes on Wednesdays, partly due to economic turmoil caused by the collapse of the country's second largest steelmaker.
But the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions still plans to go ahead with full stoppages starting on February 18 unless the government scraps a controversial new labour law, a union official said.
Hanbo Steel Co defaulted on debts last week and on Tuesday sought court protection. It is buried under a mountain of debt worth $5.8 billion.
"Korea is in turmoil due to the Hanbo incident and we have taken that into consideration," said the official, who declined to be named.

The confederation led almost four weeks of industrial stoppages against the new legislation after it was rammed through parliament on December 26. The law makes it easier for firms to lay off workers and replace strikers.
President Kim Young-sam was forced into a humiliating retreat and last week sent the bill back to parliament for revision. But he has ruled out voiding the bill.
